summary.tldr: Changes Criminal Code sentencing rules, gives courts more discretion, and requires written reasons before imposing certain minimum punishments.
what_it_does: Gives courts discretion to set the punishment when a law sets different kinds or levels of punishment for an offence, including declared minimum punishments.
Requires courts to consider all other options before imposing a minimum jail term or parole ineligibility period, and to give written reasons for that decision.
Allows courts to delay sentencing so a person found guilty can attend a treatment or counselling program under court supervision, without needing the Attorney General’s consent.
Requires judges in first and second degree murder cases to ask juries if they want to recommend parole ineligibility years, and to consider any recommendation when setting that period.
summary.background: The bill amends the Criminal Code. It changes rules about punishment, court-supervised treatment programs, and jury recommendations in murder cases.
